identity_marker: vibrant purple-red cabbage, shiny stainless steel pot, and smooth white hard-boiled eggs
continuity_anchors: brightly lit rustic kitchen with a wooden countertop, soft natural daylight streaming in, and a warm, inviting atmosphere
video_goal: Demonstrate the process of creating a natural dye from red cabbage to color white Easter eggs a vibrant blue.
single_prompt: From a top-down view, hands place a vibrant head of red cabbage onto a wooden cutting board and slice it directly in half with a chef's knife. The camera moves to a close-up as hands rapidly chop the red cabbage halves into smaller, jagged 1-inch pieces. In an over-the-shoulder view, hands scoop up the chopped red cabbage pieces and drop them into an empty stainless steel pot. A close-up shows clear water being poured from a glass pitcher into the pot, rising until it completely submerges the chopped red cabbage. From a side angle, the pot sits on a lit stove burner; the water vigorously bubbles and visibly darkens into a deep purple color. A close-up reveals a metal strainer held over a large glass bowl, and the contents of the pot are poured through it, catching the pale, boiled cabbage leaves while the dark purple liquid fills the bowl. From a top-down view, a tablespoon of clear white vinegar is poured into the steaming dark purple liquid in the glass bowl, and a metal spoon stirs the mixture in a circular motion. A close-up shows fingers placing a plain white, hard-boiled egg onto the center of a metal slotted spoon. From a side angle, the slotted spoon slowly lowers the white egg completely beneath the surface of the dark purple cabbage dye. In a top-down view, hands gently drop three more white eggs into the bowl, where they settle at the bottom of the opaque purple liquid. From an overhead view, the surface of the purple liquid becomes completely still, and shadows shift rapidly across the bowl to visually indicate the passage of several hours. A close-up shows the slotted spoon dipping into the bowl and lifting an egg out of the liquid; the egg shell is now a vibrant, pastel blue color. In an over-the-shoulder view, the spoon tilts, gently rolling the wet blue egg onto a wire cooling rack lined with white paper towels. Finally, in a macro close-up, the camera slowly pans across a finished row of four dry, naturally dyed Easter eggs, highlighting their speckled blue and teal surfaces.
